title: La Salle to the mouth of the Mississippi, and to Texas, 1682–87
summary: In 1682 La Salle took 23 Frenchmen and 18 Indigenous men down the Mississippi to the Gulf and claimed it for Louis XIV as Louisiana. In 1684 he sailed from France to found a colony at the river's mouth, but missed it by more than 370 miles and landed in Matagorda Bay, Texas. Fort Saint Louis failed, and in 1687 his own men shot him on a walk towards Illinois.

events.label: The Gulf reached, Louisiana claimed
events.source: René-Robert Cavelier, Sieur de La Salle (Wikipedia)
events.text: He raised a column and a cross and took possession of the whole river basin and every people and river in it for the king.

events.label: Fort Saint Louis, Matagorda Bay
events.source: René-Robert Cavelier, Sieur de La Salle (Wikipedia); Fort Saint Louis (Texas) (Wikipedia)
events.text: The colony was meant for the Mississippi and landed far west of it. One ship was lost on the bar, another was seized, and he built the fort inland on Garcitas Creek. Disease killed most of the settlers, and the Karankawa the rest, about Christmas 1688; in April 1689 a Spanish party found the fort in ruins and burned what remained.
